choices.question: How should I answer your phone?

options.label: Walsh Plumbing, how can I help?
options.detail: Short. Gets to the problem fast. Callers in a hurry like it.
options.rivetLine: Walsh Plumbing, how can I help?

writes.voiceGreeting: Walsh Plumbing, how can I help?

options.label: Thanks for calling Walsh Plumbing. What's going on today?
options.detail: A few more words. Feels like a front desk that knows you.
options.rivetLine: Thanks for calling Walsh Plumbing. What's going on today?

writes.voiceGreeting: Thanks for calling Walsh Plumbing. What's going on today?

choices.question: What do you charge to come out?
choices.supportLine: This is the first number a caller hears. Here's where plumbing shops in Cleveland land.

options.label: $89 to come out, then $150 an hour
options.detail: When someone asks what a water heater would run them, this is the number I give.
options.rivetLine: It's $89 for the visit, and that's credited if you go ahead with the repair.

options.label: $129 to come out, then $185 an hour
options.detail: Fewer calls, better ones. Your other prices move up with it.
options.rivetLine: It's $129 for the visit. That covers the diagnosis, and it's credited toward the repair.

choices.question: When someone wants a repair, do I book it or hold it for you?
choices.supportLine: Emergencies skip this. Those always come straight to you.

options.label: Book it on the call
options.detail: The caller leaves with a time. You get a text and one tap to undo. Nothing gets booked on top of another job.
options.rivetLine: I have Tuesday at 2 or Wednesday at 9. Which works for you?

options.label: Hold it for me
options.detail: I take the details and say you'll confirm within the hour. You tap once and I text the caller.
options.rivetLine: I've got everything I need. Jenna will confirm a time with you within the hour.

choices.question: When a job's done, how do you want to get paid?
choices.supportLine: You never have to write a bill. I make it from the job and send it. You just pick how.

options.label: Text them a pay link
options.detail: The moment you mark the job done, the customer gets a text with the bill and a pay button. Card or bank.
options.rivetLine: I'll text you the bill with a pay link as soon as the work is done.

options.label: Collect on the spot
options.detail: You take cash, check or card in the driveway. I send the receipt and keep the books straight.
options.rivetLine: You can settle up with Jenna when the work is done. I'll send your receipt right after.

choices.question: When should I put jobs on your calendar?
choices.supportLine: I'll answer every call at any hour either way. This is just when I can book.

options.label: Monday to Saturday, 7 to 5
options.detail: Six days. Most one-truck shops run this way.
options.rivetLine: I can get you on the schedule Monday through Saturday, between 7 and 5.

options.label: Weekdays, 7 to 5
options.detail: Weekends stay yours. I take messages and book Monday.
options.rivetLine: I can get you on the schedule Monday through Friday, between 7 and 5.

choices.question: Who do I ring first when it is an emergency?
choices.supportLine: Suppose a caller tells me "there's water coming through my ceiling and my dad can't get upstairs to the shutoff". Safety first, then a person. That part I always do. This part is yours.

options.label: Your cell, every time
options.detail: I patch the caller straight through and whisper what's going on before you pick up.
options.rivetLine: I'm getting Jenna on the line for you right now.

options.label: Your cell, then text you if you don't pick up
options.detail: If you miss it, the caller hears that you have been paged and I text you their number and the problem.
options.rivetLine: I'm trying Jenna now. If I can't reach them, I'll page them and they'll call you right back.

choices.question: Same call at 9pm. Do I answer and book, or take a message?
choices.supportLine: Either way an emergency still rings you.

options.label: Answer and book, any hour
options.detail: Most shops. The caller gets a real answer at 9pm and a slot for the morning.
options.rivetLine: We can have someone out first thing tomorrow. Does 8am work?

options.label: Take a message after hours
options.detail: I answer, say you're closed, and take their name and number for the morning.
options.rivetLine: We're closed for the evening. Leave your name and number and Jenna will call you first thing.

choices.question: Do customers already call a business number?
choices.supportLine: If not, the number I'm about to give you is your business number. Nothing to forward.

options.label: No, just my cell
options.detail: Your new number goes on the truck. Calls to it come to me; emergencies come to you.
options.rivetLine: You can reach Walsh Plumbing any time on this number.

options.label: Yes, I have a business line
options.detail: I'll text you a link that forwards it to me in one tap. You can do it later.
options.rivetLine: You can reach Walsh Plumbing any time on this number.
